clue.text: At first, thief only really cared for jewellery

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A burglar whose only real interest was the jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: A torc is a twisted metal neck ring worn by ancient Celts.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is an ornamental neck band, an example of jewellery.

clue.text: Visualise section of ride at Eastbourne

indicators.note: a section is only a part, so the answer is a run of letters lifted from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the first two words and into the third

explanation.surface: Picture a stretch of a seaside trip at the Sussex resort of Eastbourne.
explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form an idea or mental image, a synonym for picturing something.

clue.text: Having a few parties after cracking audition

indicators.note: something cracking another breaks into it, so it sits inside the other word

parts.note: an audition is a trial for a performer

explanation.surface: Someone who throws parties once the audition has gone well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parties' are the sides to an agreement, and 'a few' here means three, matching the tri- prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilateral treaty involves three sides, so it has a small number of participants.

clue.text: Avoid backing little Scottish boarding school? On the contrary!

indicators.note: to board is to get into something, so one piece is placed inside the other
this flips which piece boards which, so the turned-round word holds the other one
backing means going in reverse, so the word for little is read from its end

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: Steer clear of supporting a small Scottish boarding school, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the little word would board the school; 'On the contrary!' swaps the roles, so the school boards the turned-round word.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to deliberately keep away from it, a formal synonym for shun.

clue.text: Rising movement erupts violently, receiving fine

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so another piece goes inside the jumble
something done violently is thrown about, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something rises and bursts out violently while taking in fine particles.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstroke is an upward stroke of a pen or piston, a movement that goes up.

clue.text: Some savour Dutch language

indicators.note: some means only part, so the answer is taken from within the following words

parts.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: Taste some Dutch food or a bit of Dutch speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch language' looks like one phrase, but Dutch only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, an example of a tongue.

clue.text: Sport extremely inviting black French robe

parts.note: PE is physical education, school sport

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone wears a striking, inviting black French dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' looks like a verb meaning wear; it is the school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A peignoir is a woman's light dressing gown, a kind of loose robe.

clue.text: Pressure on second princess, nursed by doctor for bug

indicators.note: something nursed is held in the arms, so the following word wraps around it

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
DR is the abbreviation for doctor
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A royal under strain is cared for by a doctor for some infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' reads as an illness in this medical picture, but it is a literal insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A pond skater is a water insect that glides on the surface, and bug is a loose name for any insect.

clue.text: Heard on EastEnders, one who keeps everything calm

indicators.note: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in East London, so this means as said in a Cockney accent that drops the opening h

parts.note: someone who keeps everything is a hoarder, said without its h

explanation.surface: A soap-opera character who keeps the peace in the square.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops the h, so 'hoarder' comes out sounding like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Order as in law and order is a state of peace and quiet, a synonym for calm as a noun.

clue.text: This comic character takes to cooking porterhouse steak

indicators.note: cooking alters something's form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
takes here means takes away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the name of the cut supplies the letters
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A cartoon figure turns to grilling a big steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes to' reads as 'starts doing', but it splits: 'takes' means takes away, and 'to' is the pair of letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A superhero such as Superman is a character typical of comic books.

clue.text: Tea room returned bread

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: A tearoom sent back the loaf it was given.
explanation.definitionFit: Challah is a braided Jewish loaf eaten on the Sabbath, a type of bread.

clue.text: Did tramp originally tell Dickens to describe his simple character?

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw around it, so the two letters go around the character
originally means at the origin, so each word gives only its opening letter

parts.note: Barnaby Rudge is Dickens's simple-minded hero

explanation.surface: A question whether a vagrant first told Dickens how to write his simple-minded hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a vagrant but is the verb, walked heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge is to walk slowly and heavily, much as to tramp is.

clue.text: London borough's tendency to suppress resistance

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down, so the letter is kept inside

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A London council is inclined to stamp out any opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: Brent is a borough in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Brent is one of the 32 administrative districts of Greater London.

clue.text: Book on tree spirit is nonsense

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A book about tree spirits is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree spirit' suggests a dryad, but the two words split: a tree, then spirit as in dash and vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is senseless talk or writing, a synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: Club hit inspires teenager to start festival

parts.note: a wood is a golf club

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the letter goes inside
to start means only the beginning, so the word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A nightclub hit song moves a teenager to launch a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club hit' suggests a dance track; club is a golf club and hit is a separate verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodstock was the famous 1969 rock festival in New York State.

clue.text: Promises no cryptic compiler may use this

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscured, so these letters are disguised by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Crossword setters swear they will never use a certain trick, yet might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' sits in both halves: it rearranges the letters and describes the compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoonerism, the swapping of opening sounds, is a device setters of cryptic puzzles use in clues.

clue.text: Politician disseminating bald lie came to the heart of Surrey

indicators.note: disseminating means scattering widely, so the letters are spread into a new order
the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letters count

explanation.surface: A politician spreading a blatant falsehood arrives in the middle of a home county.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south-west of London; its six letters have two in the middle. The Liberal Democrats are a UK party.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberal Democrat is a member of that British party, so an example of a politician.

clue.text: One who's not in a union, but embraces revolutionary look

definitions.text: One who's not in a union

indicators.note: something that embraces another wraps its arms round it, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: but and bar both mean except
lo is an old word for look!

explanation.surface: A non-union worker who nevertheless cosies up to a radical image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union; it is marriage. 'But' looks like a link but supplies a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is an unmarried man, someone not joined in wedlock.

clue.text: US police arresting one with uneven array of stones

indicators.note: police arresting someone take them in, so a letter is held inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: uneven means odd, so only the odd-numbered letters are kept

explanation.surface: American cops arrest a man carrying a lopsided display of gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapidary is an adjective for things relating to gemstones or their cutting and engraving.

clue.text: Typical EU, desperate for sources of oil

indicators.note: someone desperate is in a wild state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A jibe that the European Union is predictably desperate for oil supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalyptus trees, plural here, yield the aromatic eucalyptus oil from their leaves.

clue.text: Getting ready to drop a little lower?

definitions.text: Getting ready to drop a little lower?

parts.words: Getting ready to drop a little lower?
parts.note: surface reading: preparing to sink somewhat further down

parts.words: Getting ready to drop a little lower?
parts.note: setter's reading: to drop is to give birth, and a little lower is a young animal that moos, or lows

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as more low, but here it is one who lows, like a cow; a cow about to give birth to its young is pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a cow that is pregnant and expecting to give birth.

clue.text: New decorator's more pleasant

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
one who decorates cakes with icing

explanation.surface: The new painter and decorator is an improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decorator' suggests someone painting a house; here it is someone icing a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer is the comparative of nice, so it means more agreeable.

clue.text: Picked up current deposit of ore's yield

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a vein is a seam of mineral in rock

explanation.surface: A miner collects the output of a fresh seam of ore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts a sound-alike reading; it lifts a word in this down entry. 'Yield' looks like a noun for output but means give way.
explanation.definitionFit: To cave in is to collapse or give way under pressure, a phrasal synonym for yield.

clue.text: Finish a large amount of stout, being unwilling to change

indicators.note: a large amount is most but not all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to die is to come to an end
stout and hardy both mean sturdy

explanation.surface: A drinker downs most of a pint of stout, refusing to change habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the dark beer; it is the adjective for sturdy.
explanation.definitionFit: A diehard position is stubbornly conservative, resisting any reform.

clue.text: Cases of academic negligence leading to teenager's complaint?

indicators.note: a case is an outer covering, so each word gives just its outside letters

explanation.surface: Neglect in schools causing problems for teenagers.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is the skin condition of spots that commonly afflicts adolescents.

clue.text: Boat party in Hollywood location

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Hollywood is in California, CAL for short
a rave is a lively party

explanation.surface: A party on a yacht somewhere in Hollywood.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravel is a small, fast sailing ship of the 15th–17th centuries, a kind of boat.

clue.text: Singer heads off illnesses

indicators.note: with the heads off, each word loses its first letter

parts.note: two bouts of a common virus

explanation.surface: A vocalist leaves early because of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Plural 'illnesses' gives the virus twice; each copy loses its head. Lulu is a Scottish pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lulu is the Scottish singer famous for 'Shout', so an example of a singer.

clue.text: Tatty underclothes abandoned by the dirty dog

indicators.note: tatty means shabby and worn, so the letters are in a mess
abandoned by means left behind, so those letters drop out

parts.note: taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: Shabby underwear left behind by a filthy mutt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty dog' suggests an actual animal; it is a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirty dog is an idiom for a dishonest, contemptible person, a rogue.

clue.text: Even you could make alcohol in this

definitions.meaning: first meaning: yet, as in even more or ... more

definitions.text: you could make alcohol in this
definitions.meaning: second meaning: apparatus for distilling spirits

explanation.surface: Even you would be able to brew your own booze in this.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adverb meaning yet, as in better still, and a noun for distilling equipment.
